name: Reach out to at-risk customers from Stripe and Segment events with Claude

parameters.content:
## Reach out to at-risk customers from Stripe and Segment events with Claude

**Who's it for**
Support and success teams that hear about problems only when the customer complains or leaves.

**How it works**
Trigger: Stripe/Chargebee (payment failed, trial ending), product analytics (Segment, Mixpanel, PostHog events), error monitoring (Sentry), shipping (tracking exceptions).
1. Receive or detect the signal
2. Load the customer's context
3. Decide whether to reach out
4. Draft the message
5. Approve if sensitive
6. Send on the right channel
7. Log and watch the response
8. Report what it prevented
Every AI step is followed by a "Needs a person?" gate that parks low-confidence items instead of guessing, and the write-back waits for an approval in Slack or Gmail.

**How to set up**
1. Open "Config (edit me)" and fill in the fields (names, approver, quiet hours, thresholds).
2. Add credentials to each service node.
3. Run once with test_mode on, read the output, then switch the trigger on.

**Requirements**
An Anthropic API key for the Claude nodes, plus Stripe / Chargebee, Segment / PostHog / Mixpanel, HubSpot / Intercom (or their equivalents — the nodes are standard and easy to swap).

**How to customize the workflow**
Define the trigger events and the message templates in the Config node; send through HubSpot, Intercom or Gmail. Keep the guardrail: Frequency cap: one proactive message per customer per week across all scenarios.

Full blueprint with trigger, steps, guardrails and where the standard version stops: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/proactive-customer-outreach/

## Proactive Customer Outreach Workflow

Starter template from agentmelt.com — configure before running:

1. Fill in "Config (edit me)" (name, approver, quiet hours; test_mode stays on for the first week).
2. Add credentials to every service node (Anthropic, mail, CRM, database…).
3. Replace placeholder URLs, queries and field mappings with yours.
4. Set the trigger: Stripe/Chargebee (payment failed, trial ending), product analytics (Segment, Mixpanel, PostHog events), error monitoring (Sentry), shipping (tracking exceptions). A daily Schedule Trigger scans for slow signals like feature non-adoption.
5. Keep the gates: 'Needs a person?' after every AI step, 'Approved?' after the approval — wire their dead ends to a sheet or a channel.
6. Keep the guardrails:
   - Frequency cap: one proactive message per customer per week across all scenarios.
   - Sensitive scenarios require a human click; the agent never sends about money or churn risk unattended.
   - Every message links to one action and is sent from a real inbox that receives replies.
   - Opt-outs and do-not-contact flags are honoured before any drafting happens.

Full blueprint and pricing: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/proactive-customer-outreach/
Want it built and run for you? $247/month · custom $3,500–6,000 one-time

## Steps

1. Webhook: Receive or detect the signal
2. HTTP Request: Load the customer's context
3. IF: Decide whether to reach out
4. AI Agent: Draft the message
5. Wait: Approve if sensitive
6. Gmail: Send on the right channel
7. HubSpot: Log and watch the response
8. Schedule Trigger: Report what it prevented
9. Code: Report what it prevented

Every AI step is followed by "Needs a person?"; the write-back waits for "Approved?" where the blueprint has an approval step.

Fill these in once; every later node reads them as $('Config (edit me)').item.json.config.*

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- Billing events (Stripe, Chargebee, Recurly)
- Product analytics events (Segment, Mixpanel, PostHog, Amplitude)
- Error monitoring (Sentry, Datadog)
- Shipping and order status
- CRM contact record and preferences

nodes.notes:
Load the customer's context

Plan, tenure, recent tickets, health score, account owner and communication preferences from the CRM. Customers with an open escalation or a do-not-contact flag are excluded here.

nodes.name: IF: Decide whether to reach out
nodes.notes:
Decide whether to reach out

Suppression rules: not more than one proactive message per customer per week, not during an open incident, not to accounts a CSM owns unless the CSM is copied.

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Draft the message" step of the Proactive Customer Outreach Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: From a scenario template and the context, the agent writes a short, specific message: what happened, what to do, one link. Tone and length rules are enforced by the prompt and checked by a second pass.

Rules:
- Frequency cap: one proactive message per customer per week across all scenarios.
- Sensitive scenarios require a human click; the agent never sends about money or churn risk unattended.
- Every message links to one action and is sent from a real inbox that receives replies.
- Opt-outs and do-not-contact flags are honoured before any drafting happens.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.

nodes.name: AI Agent: Draft the message
nodes.notes:
Draft the message

From a scenario template and the context, the agent writes a short, specific message: what happened, what to do, one link. Tone and length rules are enforced by the prompt and checked by a second pass.

nodes.name: Needs a person?
nodes.notes: True = the AI step was not sure or flagged the item → dead letter, a person looks. False = continue. Wire the dead letter to a Slack message or a sheet so nothing fails silently.

nodes.name: Needs a person: Draft the message
nodes.notes: Dead letter. Replace this no-op with a Slack message or a sheet row that carries the raw item and the reason — silent failures are the ones that cost.

nodes.name: Wait: Approve if sensitive
nodes.notes:
Approve if sensitive

Scenarios marked sensitive (large accounts, churn-risk, anything mentioning money) pause for a one-click approval in Slack; the rest send automatically.

nodes.name: Gmail: Send on the right channel
nodes.notes:
Send on the right channel

Email by default; in-app message via Intercom or SMS for time-critical scenarios like a delayed delivery. Sent from the support or CSM identity, never a no-reply.

nodes.name: HubSpot: Log and watch the response
nodes.notes:
Log and watch the response

The outreach is logged on the contact; replies open a ticket routed to the right person; the covered event is tracked to see whether it resolved.

nodes.name: Schedule Trigger: Report what it prevented
nodes.notes:
Report what it prevented

Weekly: for each scenario, messages sent, replies, resolution rate and — by comparison with the pre-workflow baseline — tickets avoided and payments recovered.

nodes.notes: Weekly: for each scenario, messages sent, replies, resolution rate and — by comparison with the pre-workflow baseline — tickets avoided and payments recovered.
